function.name: court_info_get_case_status
function.description: Retrieves the status and trial dates for court cases from specified county courts. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

court.description: The county court where the case is filed.

details.description: Specific details required about the court case. Defaults to 'status'.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "案件編號 XY1234 在 Los Angeles County Court 和 案件編號 GH5678 在 Orange County Court 的狀態和預定審判日期是什麼?" They want status and scheduled trial date.

We need to call the function twice? Actually we can combine into one request but likely separate calls per case. We have two queries:

1) For case XY1234 at Los Angeles County Court: get status and trial_date (both). 
2) For case GH5678 at Orange County Court: same.

But the function signature expects single query with details optional default 'status', but you can't ask both status and trial_date simultaneously unless maybe multiple calls or specify details as array? It says defaults to 'status' only; no mention of multi-details. So we might need to make two calls per case: first status then trial_date. But perhaps better to do two calls each specifying details accordingly. However we could also just use details='status' and later another call for trial_date. That would produce four calls total. Alternatively if we think the system allows us to pass an array? Not indicated. We'll assume we need separate calls.

Thus plan: Call court_info_get_case_status for XY1234, court=Los Angeles County Court, details="status". Then again same case, details="trial_date".

Then similarly for GH5678, Orange County Court.

We'll output results after retrieving all data.
